description: Composite TEM figure (panels a–f, but the label "(e)" appears twice) from an as-quenched-annealed Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.8C duplex steel, comparing undeformed and 5%-tensile-strained microstructures. (a) is a TEM micrograph, 200 nm scale bar, showing fine rounded particles labelled "(002)DO3" in ferrite, with an inset SAED pattern overlaid by a rectangular grid of diffraction spots (no indices printed). (b) is a 100 nm-scale micrograph with an arrowed label "(011)κ" marking nano κ-carbide in austenite; its inset SAED pattern is indexed 000, 010, 100, 110, 120, 210, 020γ, 220γ and 200γ. (c) is a 0.5 µm micrograph of deformed ferrite (5% strain) labelled "B2 domain" with a diffraction-vector arrow marked "002". (d) is a 100 nm micrograph of the same deformed ferrite, same "002" g arrow, labelled "Dislocation". Two panels carry "(e)": one 200 nm image with a dashed polygonal outline, and one 0.5 µm image labelled "(111)γ" and "(0̅11)κ". (f) is a low-contrast 0.5 µm image labelled "(0̅11)κ". Collectively the panels show that ordered DO3/B2 precipitates exist in ferrite and κ-carbide in austenite, and that 5% strain generates dislocations inside the B2 domain in ferrite and planar slip features in austenite.

observations.observation: Panel (a) carries the phase label '(002)DO3' and a 200 nm scale bar, consistent with fine DO3 particles imaged in ferrite.
Panel (a) contains an inset SAED pattern with a rectangular grid drawn over the diffraction spots, but no spot indices or zone-axis label are printed.
Panel (b) marks nano κ-carbide in austenite with an arrow and the label '(011)κ' at a 100 nm scale bar.
The SAED inset of panel (b) is indexed with the reflections 000, 010, 100, 110, 120, 210, 020γ, 220γ and 200γ, mixing κ and γ (fcc) spots.
Panels (c) and (d) are deformed-ferrite micrographs both annotated with a diffraction vector arrow marked '002'; (c) is additionally labelled 'B2 domain' and (d) 'Dislocation'.
The figure contains two distinct panels labelled '(e)' — one with a 200 nm scale bar and one with a 0.5 µm scale bar — so the panel lettering is non-unique/redundant.
Panel (e) [200 nm] shows a dashed white polygonal outline delimiting a planar/banded deformation feature, with no phase label printed.
The caption states that (a) shows fine DO3 particles in ferrite and (b) nano κ-carbide in austenite.
The caption states that (c, d) show the deformed ferrite microstructure at 5% strain, with dislocations inside the B2 domain.
The caption states that (e, f) show the deformed austenite microstructure at 5% strain, and that the figure covers the microstructure before and after tensile deformation.
The citing text states the steel is a Fee27Mne12Ale0.8C A-BDP steel with a 27% δ-ferrite fraction investigated by Park et al. [91].
The citing text states that coarse B2 and ultrafine DO3 particles precipitated in ferrite, while nano κ-carbide precipitated in austenite and coarsened with increasing ordering-annealing temperature.

The citing text states that during tensile deformation the κ-carbide in austenite is sheared by plane-slip dislocations, whereas in ferrite super-dislocations interact with narrow mechanical reverse domain boundaries.

subfigures.description: TEM micrograph, 200 nm scale bar, showing fine rounded/particulate features labelled '(002)DO3' in a mottled ferrite matrix, interpreted as fine DO3 particles in ferrite. An inset SAED pattern is overlaid with a rectangular reciprocal-lattice grid of bright spots; no spot indices are printed.

TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, with an arrow pointing to a labelled feature '(011)κ' (nano κ-carbide in austenite). The inset SAED pattern shows discrete spots annotated 220γ, 020γ, 120, 210, 110, 010, 100, 200γ and 000.

TEM micrograph of deformed ferrite after 5% strain, 0.5 µm scale bar, labelled 'B2 domain'; a white arrow marks the diffraction vector g = 002. Dense intersecting dislocation lines form a cell/domain-like network.
Higher-magnification TEM micrograph of deformed ferrite, 100 nm scale bar, with the same g = 002 arrow and the text label 'Dislocation'; dark curved dislocation lines run across the field.
TEM micrograph, 200 nm scale bar, showing a heavily deformed structure with a dashed white polygonal outline delineating a banded/planar feature. No phase labels are printed on this panel.
TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar, labelled '(111)γ' (with arrow) and '(0̅11)κ', showing a lamellar/banded deformed austenite structure with parallel slip traces.
Low-contrast TEM micrograph, 0.5 µm scale bar, labelled '(0̅11)κ'; faint parallel bands and dark linear traces are visible against a finely mottled background.
